messages.subject: observeEvent in a loop
parts:
Hi, I want to generate dynamic UI (several actionButtons) according to a file (aa.txt). And each button is observed to generate a unique plot. I tried to embed observeEvent in a loop
to observe the dynamic buttons but failed. It turned out that only the last button was observed. Is there any way to fix this?
Thanks!

here is the server.R



library(shiny)


shinyServer(function(input,output, session){


tableNames <- read.table("aa.txt", header = FALSE, stringsAsFactor = FALSE)[ , 1]


output$buttAll <- renderUI({


        LL <- list()


        length(LL) <- length(tableNames)


        for(i in 1:length(tableNames)){


        LL[[i]] <- list(actionButton(paste0("runButton", i), tableNames[i]))


        }


        return(LL)


        })


output$ck1 <- renderPlot({

       for(i in 1:length(tableNames)){

           observeEvent(input[[paste0("runButton", i)]],

               {

                hist(rnorm(100, mean = i, sd = 2))

               }

                         )

       }

})

})


ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(


pageWithSidebar(


    headerPanel("Graph"),


    sidebarPanel(

       textInput("text_input_fingerprints", "Query"),

               uiOutput("buttAll")

   ),


    mainPanel(

   tabsetPanel(

     tabPanel('plot',

              plotOutput("cdk1", height = 1000, width = 1000))

               )

       )




   )


   )


  )

Hi,

I would use a global variable to store the button values, like

library(shiny)

button <- new.env()
button$labels   <- letters[1:5]
button$inputIds <- sprintf("button%i", 1:length(button$labels))
button$presses  <- rep(0, length(button$labels))

ui <- fluidPage(
    uiOutput("buttonUI"),
    hr(),
    textOutput("print")
)

server <- function(input, output){

    output$buttonUI <- renderUI({
        lob <- list()
        for (i in 1:length(button$labels))
            lob[[i]] <- actionButton(inputId=button$inputIds[i],
                                     label=button$labels[i])
        lob
    })
   
    output$print <- renderPrint({
      for (i in 1:length(button$labels)) {
        buttoni <- input[[button$inputIds[i]]]
        if (!is.null(buttoni)) {
          button.pressed <- (buttoni>button$presses[i])
          if (button.pressed) {
            print(sprintf("Button '%s' pressed", button$labels[i]))
            button$presses[i] <- buttoni
          }
        }
      }
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Best Sigbert

messages.author: 2b46f14139c84304
messages.subject: Re: observeEvent in a loop
parts:
Hi,

I guess it is because renderForceNetwork expects a result of type "forceNetwork" as "return". Since only one button can be pressed at a specific time, store the return and deliver it at then end of the expression, e.g.

output$print <- renderForceNetwork({
      ret <- NULL;

for (i in 1:length(button$labels)) {
        buttoni <- input[[button$inputIds[i]]]
        if (!is.null(buttoni)) {
          button.pressed <- (buttoni>button$presses[i])
          if (button.pressed) {

button$presses[i] <- buttoni
           ret <- forceNetwork(Links  = MisLinks, Nodes = MisNodes,

Source = "source", Target = "target",
                               Value  = "value", NodeID = "name",
                               Group = "group", opacity = 0.8)
          }
        }
      }

ret
  })
}



Best Sigbert
